ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law); Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (including the 2016 SCSprules); Law of 23 July 2016 implementing the SCSp; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2016 on transparency and the RBE; CSSF Circular 15/01 and related AML/CFT regulatory framework; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and the Register of Commerce and Companies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) or authentic copy of the SCSp limited partnership agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (in case of authentic deed) or duly appointed counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic deed does not require apostille; foreign-language exhibits must be notarized, translated into French/German/English, and, if executed abroad, apostilled under the Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of each corporate general partner or limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce and Companies of the partner's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (depending on state of origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney to execute formation and registration documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for foreign-signed PoAs

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/KYC file for UBOs (passport, proof of address, source of wealth statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or Luxembourg approved resident agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization with apostille/consular legalization where origin is foreign; validation of residency and identity documentation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, partners, directors, and relevant officers against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Luxembourg national sanctions list, and publicly available PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence required for PEPs, individuals connected to sanctioned jurisdictions, and any unusual ownership patterns. Continuous monitoring obligations apply under the AML/CFT Law; client files must be retained for at least five years after the close of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the LBR e-Platform (www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be written in Latin script; the language of the name may be French, German, English, Luxembourgish, or another Latin-script language, but the statutory filing text must be in one of the official legal languages (French or German) or accompanied by a certified translation. Names must be distinguishable from existing RCS registrations and must not infringe protected designations or public order. If the entity will use a DevTools cloud trade name outside Luxembourg, transliteration to Latin alphabet is mandatory.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may submit an administrative appeal to the RCS Registry Commissioner within 15 days of the rejection notice; the appeal must set out the grounds in writing and may include a revised proposed name. If the Registry maintains the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within the statutory deadline of one month from notification. A name reservation may be extended for a further 30-day period by filing a renewal request with LBR before the initial reservation expires, provided no competing filing has intervened.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are conditionally permissible for an SCSp used as a passive holding or treasury entity if a registered agent maintains the official address and if no substantive operational activity takes place. For an SCSp actually conducting business operations under ISIC 6201 as a developer infrastructure and cloud service provider, physical premises in Luxembourg are expected to meet commercial-substance requirements; a pure virtual mailbox may jeopardize tax rulings and the availability of reduced withholding rates under certain DTAAs.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a passive SCSp holding (estimated 3–8% annual inspection probability). Moderate to elevated for an active SCSp with employees, physical infrastructure, or Luxembourg-source cloud service revenue (estimated 10–20% annual inspection probability by RCS, social security authorities, and tax administration).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), notably Articles 103-1 et seq. on the special limited partnership, together with Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the SCSp; RCS registration provisions and allied transparency rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société / acte de constitution) filed with the RCS first-registration application (première immatriculation), followed by publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up or share capital applies to an SCSp. Contributions are contractually agreed in the partnership agreement and may be capital or non-cash commitments. No statutory escrow account, bank certificate, or capital attestation is required at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. The initial subscriptions and contribution commitments of the limited partners to the SCSp partnership agreement, as set out in the contribution schedule, are hereby approved and accepted by the general partner. 2. The registered office of the SCSp is fixed at [●], Luxembourg, and the general partner is authorised to execute and file all registration documents with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and to arrange publication in the RESA. 3. [Name] is appointed initial manager of the SCSp, with sole signature authority for ordinary management, incorporation, banking and tax filings. 4. [Name] is appointed the initial AML/KYC and tax representative. 5. All actions taken in furtherance of these resolutions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute SCSp partnership agreement and complete KYC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public if used; otherwise private deed executed by the initial partners without public authority filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the SCSp partnership agreement in French or English. SCSp formation is by private writing; a notarial deed is required only when a partner contributes Luxembourg real estate or when another mandatory notarisation event occurs. All general and limited partners must sign, and corporate partners must attach resolution extracts and authorised signatory evidence. Foreign public documents must be apostilled or legalised and translated into French or English.
required_dossiers: Passports or identity cards of all partners
Proof of address of each partner
Certificate of incorporation and board resolution for each corporate partner
Apostille or legalisation of foreign corporate documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or professional adviser raises KYC or document deficiencies, provide corrected exhibits within five business days. The private deed remains valid once all signatories and supporting documents are perfected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt constitutive governance resolutions and appoint general partner and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private act of the initial partners; no registry filing at this stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the constitutive meeting and adopt written resolutions approving the partnership agreement, fixing the registered office, appointing the general partner and manager, confirming contribution schedules, and delegating authority to open bank accounts and file the RCS application. Obtain written acceptance from the manager and domiciliation service provider.
required_dossiers: Written resolutions of the initial partners
Acceptance deed of the general partner and manager
Identity documents and specimen signatures of authorised signatories
Consent of the registered office provider (siège social approval)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a corporate general partner lacks valid authorisation, obtain a certified board resolution and recent excerpt from its home commercial register before proceeding to the RCS step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File first registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS electronic filing portal (www.lbr.lu).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS first-registration application containing the SCSp's name, legal form, registered office, corporate object, duration, general partner, managers, and signatories. Attach the signed partnership agreement and registered-office consent as PDFs. Pay the official RCS filing fee online. Once verified, the RCS issues the registration certificate and triggers publication in the RESA.
required_dossiers: Signed SCSp partnership agreement in PDF
Identification and specimen signatures of authorised persons
Declaration of no prior prohibition or conviction for the general partner and manager, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (demande de régularisation), correct the registration form, translation, or missing exhibit within the RCS deadline and resubmit online. The registration becomes effective only upon issuance of the RCS certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register beneficial owners in the Luxembourg RBE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE), managed by Luxembourg Business Registers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the confidential beneficial-ownership declaration using the RBE e-filing service. Identify each natural person who directly or indirectly holds more than 25% of the SCSp interests or otherwise exercises ultimate control. Maintain the declaration current and file any subsequent changes within the statutory period.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of ultimate beneficial owners
Declaration of percentage of interest or control
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE communicates an observation, verify the ownership percentages and resubmit a corrected declaration promptly. Late or incomplete RBE filings may attract administrative sanctions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for income tax; online filing via MyGuichet (guichet.public.lu) and Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) portal for entity registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SCSp established or operated by foreign participants, the general partner (commandité) must first register the partnership in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS). The AEDT then assigns a Luxembourg national business number and, where taxable activities are performed, a VAT identification number. Non-resident suppliers without a fixed establishment in Luxembourg must submit Form 010/1 (VAT registration) plus certified constitutional documents of the foreign entity, proof of appointment of the general partner, a Luxembourg tax representative appointment if requiring one, identity and residency documents of the partners, and a statement describing the intended economic activities. The SCSp itself may be registered for VAT if it independently carries out taxable activities; otherwise the partners are jointly liable. For income tax, the ACD issues a local income tax file reference upon first tax filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the SCSp is fiscally transparent under Luxembourg domestic law; income, gains, and withholding tax treatment are determined at the partner level. Resident corporate partners are taxed on their worldwide income, while non-resident partners are taxable only on Luxembourg-source income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or on specific Luxembourg-source items. The entity does not automatically incur corporate income tax unless an opaque election is made.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg tax law allows an SCSp to elect to be treated as opaque for direct tax purposes, i.e. to be subject to corporate income tax and municipal business tax, provided that all partners with unlimited liability are Luxembourg-resident corporate entities or all partners are corporate entities. The election is binding for at least five fiscal years and requires taxation in the hands of the partnership as if it were a company. For US federal tax purposes, the SCSp may separately make a check-the-box election under Form 8832, and hybrid mismatch considerations under ATAD II apply to elections producing double-non-taxation or deduction/non-inclusion outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA) — EU-harmonised value added tax system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR — Luxembourg-established businesses are exempt from VAT if annual taxable turnover remains below EUR 35,000 (excluding VAT) under the small-business franchise; non-established foreign suppliers are required to register from the very first taxable transaction or intra-Community acquisition, with no de minimis threshold. For intra-EU distance sales and digital services, special schemes (OSS) apply above an EU-wide threshold of EUR 10,000, but for an SCSp in cloud DevOps infrastructure, registration is mandatory whenever Luxembourg place-of-supply rules produce a taxable supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently imposes no general real-time e-invoicing clearance, no mandatory digital stamping, and no API-based pre-approval for B2B or B2C invoices. B2B e-invoicing is permitted under buyer consent or self-billing agreements. For public-sector invoices (B2G), e-invoices must be transmitted in PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format through the Luxembourg eProcurement platform. VAT returns are filed electronically on a monthly, quarterly, or annual basis via MyGuichet, and the AEDT may request SAF-T-like electronic audit files.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Luxembourg VAT law zero-rates exports of goods transported to non-EU countries under Article 16 of the VAT Act, allowing the exporter to apply 0% and retain the immediate right to deduct input VAT, provided the exporter is VAT-identified and holds conclusive evidence that the goods left the EU within the legal period (usually 90 days from dispatch). Services, including digital infrastructure and DevOps cloud tools, supplied to non-EU business customers fall outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule, so no output VAT is charged; the supplier must substantiate the customer's non-EU business establishment through an EU VAT number, corporate registration extract, or written confirmation, and retain invoice and usage records showing where the service is actually supplied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Single Administrative Document (SAD) / customs export declaration (D.E. 01) endorsed by the departing customs office
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or CMR international transport consignment note
Commercial invoice referencing the SAD and the customer VAT/registration numbers
Packing list detailing the goods and final destination
Inward remittance certificate / SWIFT bank payment confirmation evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Proof of movement: transport contract, truck transit documents, and proof of arrival at the third-country destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are closely scrutinised by the AEDT. If supporting documentation is incomplete, falsified, or not obtained within the legal time limits, the sale is reclassified as taxable at the standard 15% rate, with interest charged at 0.6% per month or part-month and assessed up to the applicable limitation period (5 years ordinary, 10 years in cases of fraud). Administrative penalties range from EUR 250 to EUR 12,500 per misdeclared invoice, and intentional falsification of export evidence may constitute tax fraud, carrying criminal penalties of up to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to EUR 12,500 per count.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as the national monetary authority, with monetary policy competence vested in the European Central Bank (ECB) as Luxembourg is a euro-area member state. The Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the prudential and AML/CFT supervisor for credit institutions, payment institutions and electronic money institutions. The BCL operates TARGET2 and SEPA clearing settlement for euro-denominated payments and oversees the smooth functioning of payment, clearing and securities settlement systems in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Luxembourg applies the EU free movement of capital and payments regime under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Directive 88/361/EEC; there are no exchange controls, no restrictions on current account or capital account transactions, and no licensing requirement for foreign exchange operations by non-bank corporates. For the SCSp, profit remittance is unhindered: because the Société en Commandite Spéciale is tax-transparent and lacks separate legal personality, income flows through to its partners without Luxembourg withholding tax at entity level, and partners resident or non-resident may freely receive distributions, provided the partnership is not engaged in regulated financial services. Practical hurdles are limited to banking KYC documentation of each partner and, where capital is mobilised from non-EEA jurisdictions, compliance with EU sanctions screening and OECD CRS/FATCA reporting obligations. Inward direct investment and repatriation of invested capital, liquidation proceeds and operational surpluses are not subject to prior administrative approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg and the euro area impose no export proceeds surrender, conversion quota or repatriation deadline on commercial receipts. The SCSp may retain 100% of its export earnings from software subscriptions, developer infrastructure licensing, database monitoring services and API usage fees, in EUR or in any foreign currency, held on accounts with EU/EEA credit institutions or authorised payment/electronic-money institutions. The only statutory constraints are general corporate record-keeping obligations and CSSF AML/CFT requirements to demonstrate the economic substance and source of funds of commercial flows if using foreign-currency accounts or contracting with counterparties in higher-risk jurisdictions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency EUR/USD) and Capital Escrow Account (Séquestre)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for payment collection but Low as the sole treasury rail. Stripe Payments Europe Ltd (Ireland), an electronic money institution authorised by the Central Bank of Ireland, may passport into Luxembourg under PSD2 via the CSSF and operate the Stripe_Billing rail for card acquiring and SEPA Direct Debit collection; it is a compliant collection front-end but cannot provide deposit-taking, escrow, commercial lending or FX hedging. Mercury (US) is a US fintech that offers ACH through partner banks such as Evolve Bank & Trust; it is not licensed in the EU, cannot issue SEPA/EUR IBANs to a Luxembourg entity and cannot lawfully hold euro deposits for EU customers. Direct use of Mercury_ACH by the LU SCSp is therefore Low viability and raises Luxembourg payment-services-law concerns (Law of 10 November 2009 transposing PSD2) unless ACH is channelled through a separately registered US group entity whose USD balances are subsequently swept to Luxembourg by SWIFT MT103. The structurally correct model is: Stripe for global card/SEPA collection, a US LLC (disregarded for Luxembourg purposes under appropriate substance safeguards) for US ACH, and a Luxembourg Tier-1 bank for EUR/USD treasury concentration, escrow and hedging.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML law (Law of 12 November 2004, Article 3, as amended; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF AML/CFT circulars) does not strictly mandate in-person appearance when reliable remote identification is performed through eIDAS-qualified video verification; remote account opening is accepted in practice for the Low_Risk_Standard category. However, because the SCSp has no separate legal personality and acts through its general partner(s), the bank must identify the Gérant (or all general partners) and every beneficial owner above 25%. Most Tier-1 Luxembourg banks will accept a remote video interview plus certified passport copies and a notarially legalised partnership deed, but practically require one physical meeting of the Gérant or a named manager of a corporate general partner, either at the bank or before a Luxembourg notary/regulated fiduciary (CSF), before activating outbound disbursement and FX lines. Directors of the corporate general partner should be prepared to attend an in-person or high-grade video KYC interview within two weeks of application submission.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: SCSp lacks separate legal personality, creating ambiguity over who legally binds the entity and who holds the funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) fully executed partnership agreement (contrat de société) under the Law of 12 July 2013 on the SCSp, (ii) certificate of registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), (iii) authorisation of the Gérant to open bank accounts including specimen signature powers, (iv) if the general partner is a legal entity, its constitutional documents, board resolution and register of directors, and (v) any delegation of authority to the fund administrator or payment processor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: opacity of beneficial ownership due to multi-layer non-resident investor chain and the tax-transparent nature of the partnership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (i) the mandatory beneficial-owner filing with the Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) made within one month of incorporation, (ii) an ownership and control chart identifying all individuals holding directly or indirectly more than 25% of capital or voting rights, (iii) passport copies and proof of residential address, (iv) CV or professional biography for each material UBO, and (v) a written source-of-wealth memorandum signed by the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: re-characterisation of the SCSp as a regulated collective investment undertaking or professional fund, triggering fund licences rather than an operating company account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (i) the ISIC 6201 business plan evidencing active DevOps infrastructure, database monitoring and API tooling business, (ii) customer contracts, website/API terms of service and recurring-revenue evidence, (iii) an opinion from Luxembourg counsel confirming the SCSp is not an undertaking for collective investment within the meaning of Part II of the Law of 17 December 2010, and (iv) confirmation that the SCSp holds no investor subscriptions outside identified operating partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: use of a US fintech (Mercury) and an Irish EMI (Stripe) raises suspicion of unlicensed payment services or unbanked settlement flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) the signed payment-processing agreement with Stripe Payments Europe Ltd evidencing regulated EMI status and PSD2 passporting notice, (ii) the Mercury partner-bank disclosure (Evolve Bank & Trust, FDIC-insured) restricted to a US group entity, (iii) a memorandum confirming the SCSp merely subscribes to third-party payment services and does not hold client funds as a principal, and (iv) a diagram showing settlement paths from Stripe and Mercury into the Luxembourg bank accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: capital injections from high-risk or non-sanctioned but opaque jurisdictions, or mismatches in transfer purpose codes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (i) a capital call notice and investor subscription documents matching each incoming wire, (ii) source-of-funds evidence consisting of six months of bank statements at the investor level, (iii) tax residence certificates and CRS self-certification forms, (iv) negative media and sanctions-screening reports certified by a Luxembourg fiduciary, and (v) an undertaking that any future investor deposits below EUR 10,000 or above EUR 50,000 will trigger enhanced due diligence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from EU/EEA investors are routed by SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT or SCT Inst) to the SCSp's EUR operational or escrow account at the Luxembourg bank, using ISO 20022 purpose code 'CAPT' (payment of capital) or 'INVS' (investment) and the remittance information block showing the SCSp name, the capital call reference and the investor identifier. Non-EEA (typically US) investors remit via SWIFT MT103 from their bank, converted to EUR by the Luxembourg bank under a standing FX instruction if needed; the MT103 must carry the beneficiary IBAN, the exact legal name 'LU SCSp' or the full partnership name, and purpose description 'Capital Contribution' referencing the partnership agreement and the notarised RCS excerpt. The receiving bank performs sanctions screening against OFAC and EU restricted-party lists and reconciles each credit against the updated partner register; funds whose origin does not match a documented partner are suspended pending source-of-funds evidence. Where initial commitments are pari-passu locked at closing, the bank operates a capital escrow (séquestre) account with dual-signatory release against the signed capital call and the RBE filing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EEA software, database and API infrastructure vendors, the rail is SEPA Credit Transfer settled through TARGET2 or a SEPA-compliant CSM, with reference codes aligned to the invoice. For non-EEA disbursements — principally US cloud providers (AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure) and global subprocessors — the Luxembourg bank executes a SWIFT MT103 in USD through its US correspondent over Fedwire or CHIPS, debiting the SCSp's EUR account and applying a spot EUR/USD conversion. Larger infrastructure procurement (annual committed-use contracts or custom hardware/network gear) may be supported by a commercial documentary letter of credit or standby letter of credit issued on behalf of the SCSp, especially where the supplier requires payment against shipping or delivery documents. Stripe settlement is pulled or pushed in EUR to the SCSp's bank account on a daily roll-up basis; USD ACH proceeds generated through a US group entity on Mercury are swept by SWIFT wire at regular intervals to Luxembourg to avoid trapped USD liquidity. The SCSp is advised to maintain a small USD working-capital account at the Luxembourg bank to absorb timing mismatches between USD ACH inflow and USD vendor bills.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD outright FX forward contracts with a regulated EU credit institution (maturity up to 12 months) under an ISDA 2002 or short-form FX master agreement
FX swaps (spot-forward and forward-forward) used for treasury rollovers and liquidity conversion between USD and EUR
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (EUR/USD CCS) if the SCSp enters asset-liability management mismatches exceeding EUR 10 million equivalent
Vanilla European-style FX options (EUR/USD call/put) purchased for downside protection, with premium paid upfront and no margin top-up requirement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) exclusively for restricted or non-convertible emerging-market currencies where the cloud/developer-tools business invoices local distributors; USD and EUR NDFs are not market-consistent and should be avoided
Exchange-traded currency futures and FX ETFs (EUR/USD) as a low-documentation alternative if bilateral ISDA credit support is refused

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Trade and Companies Register (RCS/RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year-end; calendar-year SCSp must file by 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may incur fines up to EUR 1,000 plus publication costs; repeated non-filing empowers the Public Prosecutor to seek judicial dissolution and administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership (RBE) confirmation and partner-interest update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within one month of the LBR annual reminder; any transfer of partnership interests affecting beneficial ownership must be declared within one month of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance attracts criminal fines up to EUR 1.25 million and imprisonment up to 5 years for the general partner or managers; persistent default does not independently trigger strike-off but blocks RCS filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax information return and municipal business tax declaration (SCSp transparency filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Luxembourg Inland Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year partnerships: due by 31 December of the following year under ACD e-filing practice; non-calendar fiscal years: within six months after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties start at EUR 250 and may escalate up to EUR 10,000; tax authority may proceed to subsequent assessment; no direct effect on administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is required if the SCSp qualifies as a large undertaking under Article 69 of the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915, exceeding for two consecutive financial years any two of: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average headcount 50. Audit is also mandatory if the SCSp is authorized by the CSSF as an alternative investment fund or if required by its partnership agreement or an investor covenant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 10 August 1915 and EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for statutory annual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must keep an up-to-date register of partners and file all changes to beneficial ownership with the RBE within one month. Annually, the general partner must confirm the RBE data under penalty of criminal sanctions; any transfer of partnership interests that changes a 25% or greater beneficial owner must be declared, not merely confirmed, within one month of completion.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (partners' and board meeting minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 20,000 if audit obligation triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% national corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, IRC); a 7% solidarity surcharge is levied on the IRC amount and municipal business tax of 6.75% applies in Luxembourg City, producing a combined marginal effective burden of approximately 24.94% for a taxable Luxembourg collective entity. The SCSp itself is fiscally transparent (pass-through) and bears no IRC, municipal business tax or net wealth tax on its profits; the tax burden crystallizes at the level of the general and limited partners according to their residence and treaty position.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box regime: 80% exemption of qualifying net income derived from computer programs, software copyrights and qualifying API/DevOps IP, subject to the modified nexus ratio; for 2025 the combined effective rate on qualifying software IP income is approximately 4.99%. Participation exemption: 100% exemption for qualifying dividend income and realized capital gains on qualifying participations (minimum 10% interest or EUR 1,200,000 acquisition cost, 12-month holding period and subject-to-tax condition). Additional reliefs: R&D tax credit for software research expenditures, accelerated depreciation on qualifying intangible assets, and the pass-through characterization of the SCSp enabling partners to offset personal losses, deductions and treaty credits. No general statutory tax holiday exists, but Luxembourg offers structural incentives superior to formal holidays for cloud/DevTools operators.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 610 (Déclaration collective en matière d'impôt sur le revenu, d'impôt commercial communal et d'impôt sur la fortune) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu and the eCDF portal of the Administration des Contributions Directes; a transparent SCSp files an informational/nil return in practice when carrying on Luxembourg-source commercial activity, whereas a taxable corporate partner files Form 610 proportionally for its allocable share.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Quarterly CIT prepayments are due on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December of the tax year; the annual declaration is filed once per fiscal year after year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual tax return must be filed by 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end (a 31 December year-end therefore requires filing by 31 December of the immediately following year). Extensions are available only on formal written demand. Any assessed tax is payable within two months of the assessment notice; failure to pay triggers monthly delay interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification data of the entity: legal name of the SCSp, RCS registration number, registered office, fiscal year-end, general partner identity and activities under ISIC 6201.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners do not file this section; where the SCSp is transparent, the Luxembourg declarant schedules the partner names and residence countries only for the informational statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross global turnover: SaaS/API subscriptions, usage-based metering revenue, monitoring platform fees, infrastructure licensing proceeds and incidental sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source turnover that remains allocable to a permanent establishment outside Luxembourg is reportable only as a deduction/exclusion if the applicable DTA allocation is documented; no DTA reallocation is permissible for offshore invoicing without substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: cloud hosting, colocation, engineer compensation, equipment depreciation, software licenses, external contractors, and intercompany charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Charges paid or received from non-resident related parties must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; treaty-exempt items must be isolated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of qualifying income derived from software IP (copyrights, API standardization patents, proprietary monitoring algorithms) after application of the modified nexus ratio, with 80% of qualifying net profit exempted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IP Box ratio requires Luxembourg qualifying expenditure within the SCSp economically owned in Luxembourg; a non-resident partner may benefit only through its allocable partnership share and must prove beneficial ownership in a treaty claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward utilization: offset of prior-year tax losses against current profits, with municipal business tax carryforward limited to a five-year window in the computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The pass-through entity reports the loss allocation to each partner; foreign partners apply home-country carryforward rules, and Luxembourg DTA relief is not available for domestic losses twice used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of current-year profit/loss to each general and limited partner, including percentage, amount, and distributed/undistributed character.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A partner's net taxable Luxembourg profit remains subject to Luxembourg taxation only if attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg-source IP; residence certificates must be attached.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing after formal notice triggers a surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax (minimum EUR 25), monthly delay interest at 0.8% per commenced month, and an administrative penalty of up to EUR 25,000; repeated or fraudulent non-filing can result in criminal prosecution with fines up to EUR 150,000 and imprisonment of the responsible officers up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on profit distributions by an SCSp: the vehicle is fiscally transparent and payments to partners are recharacterized as direct allocations, not dividends subject to Luxembourg withholding. In contrast, a classical Luxembourg holding company remains subject to the 15% domestic dividend withholding tax, reducible to 5% under a standard participation DTA clause, to 0% under the full participation exemption where the 12-month holding condition is met, and to 0% within the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive framework when the parent holds at least 10% for 12 uninterrupted months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the partner must submit to the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) a protective reclaim together with the annually issued Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the partner's competent authority, evidence of beneficial ownership, holding period, and substance. Luxembourg applies treaty relief either at source after obtaining pre-clearance, or through a refund reclaim filed within three years of the flow; the EU Parent-Subsidiary and Interest/Royalty Directives operate directly when the statutory participation and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied; processing generally takes 6 to 12 months, with statutory delay interest payable by the tax administration if the assessment timeframe is exceeded.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding on outbound royalties and interest is 0% in Luxembourg; Luxembourg does not levy a withholding tax on arm's length royalty or interest payments to non-resident enterprises. However, treaty-combined exposure may arise in the source jurisdiction of the payer; Luxembourg ACD strictly applies Article 56 LIR abuse limitations where royalty/interest flows are artificially routed to obtain a tax advantage. Director fees and certain deemed payments carry specific 20% to 30% wage withholding obligations where paid through Luxembourg payroll.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory filing threshold in EUR applies; administrative practice under the Luxembourg transfer pricing circular (A.C.D. circular L.I.R. n° 56/1 of 28 January 2011) expects contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation once cross-border controlled transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 per year, or EUR 300,000 for pure financing transactions; a de facto zero threshold applies where the SCSp lacks a fixed office, local employees and risk-bearing capacity.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations statute; substance is instead enforced through the General Anti-Abuse Rule, ATAD 1 and ATAD 2 CFC rules, the 2013 transfer pricing circular, and the 2020 QIE substance circular. An SCSp operating DevOps/cloud infrastructure must demonstrate local governance, qualified personnel in Luxembourg, physical or leased IT infrastructure, revenue-generating decision autonomy, and actual risk control to benefit from DTA rates, the IP Box, the participation exemption, and the interest/royalty directive protections. A letterbox partnership is disregarded and re-attributed to the place of effective management of its controlling partner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underdeclaration of SaaS/API subscriptions, suppression of usage-meter data, use of undisclosed Stripe Billing or Mercury ACH accounts, creation of false invoices, or backdating of contracts to conceal Luxembourg-source cloud revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of evaded IRC and municipal business tax with a 50% fraud surcharge on the evaded amount, monthly late-payment interest at 0.8%, fines up to EUR 150,000, imprisonment of responsible officers up to 5 years for aggravated tax fraud, and public debarment from regulated procurement and cloud accreditation schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of the SCSp veil where the partnership was fully owned and asset-stripped: active general partners face civil restitution of the evaded tax plus interest; the managing partner is exposed to travel bans in cross-border EU enforcement and imprisonment for up to five years; personal disqualification as a Luxembourg fiscal representative is automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp registered as a Special LP with no Luxembourg office, zero local personnel, no local bank account, IP nominally 'owned' by a foreign affiliate, and all material decisions taken remotely by non-resident beneficial owners; use of the structure purely to obtain Luxembourg treaty or IP Box advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA reduced rates and domestic participation exemption; disallowance of the IP Box; re-taxation of the SCSp as a resident entity managed in Luxembourg; reassessment with a 20% late-filing surcharge; exchange of information triggered by foreign authorities resulting in a mirror adjustment and double taxation on the foreign partner side.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil piercing exposes the general partner's personal assets for the full reassessed tax; civil fines of EUR 25,000 per responsible officer; travel bans ordered by the home tax authority in parallel enforcement; the compliance director may be criminally charged for facilitating a cross-border artificial arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file beneficial ownership data with the Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs within one month of incorporation; absence of AML/KYC files on payment rail beneficiaries of Stripe Billing and Mercury ACH; distribution of funds to unverified non-resident limited partners; omission of the general partner's personal data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 14,000 for each UBO register omission under the amended AML law of 13 January 2019, escalating to EUR 250,000 for systemic institutional failure; CSSF/CRF freezing orders on bank and payment accounts; prohibition of profit distributions until the files are remediated; increased scrutiny under the 5th and 6th EU AML Directives.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The compliance officer and general partner are jointly liable for AML fines; criminal imprisonment of up to 2 years for laundering the proceeds of a fraudulent subscription scheme; travel bans and asset freezes applied in cross-border AML investigations after mutual recognition of confiscation orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Imposing artificial royalty or management fees on the SCSp; forcing the Luxembourg entity into a zero-margin position; undocumented intercompany pricing for API hosting, database monitoring or infrastructure resale transactions; mispricing hard-to-value intangibles without an existing Advance Pricing Agreement or robust benchmarking study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustments under Article 56 LIR with recalculation of the arm's length result via TNMM or profit split; monthly late-payment interest at 0.8% on the upward adjustment; additional 10% penalty on the reassessed base; referral to EU joint transfer pricing arbitration; consequential DTA relief denial causes double taxation within EU/PEA frameworks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed false transfer pricing documentation are exposed to negligence liability for the avoided tax amount; falsification of commercial books carries imprisonment up to 5 years; travel bans applied under cross-border enforcement directives; disqualification from acting as fiscal representative or partnership manager in Luxembourg.
